children: Crude futures post gains with a Houthi attack on the headquarters of Saudi Aramco and further strikes on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz keeping geopolitical risk premium high. Heightened tensions "are apt to curtail tanker movement through the Strait of Hormuz while at the same time, demanding an even larger risk premium to account for the possibility of renewed disruptions through the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait," Ritterbusch & Associates says in a note. U.S. inventory data on Thursday are expected to show a small crude stock build and declines in gasoline and diesel, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. The report will likely reflect the impact on offshore production from Hurricane Isaias. Output was almost fully restored by Wednesday, according to the Marine Mineral Administration. WTI settles up 1% at $95.09 a barrel and Brent gains 0.4% to $106.06.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
